name: Zell Miller Grant
summary: Pays full standard tuition for Georgia residents in a technical certificate or diploma program at a TCSG or USG school. No high school GPA or test score is needed to start, but students must keep a 3.5 college GPA.
how_to_apply: Complete the FAFSA or Georgia's state aid application (GSFAPPS) on GAfutures and enroll in an eligible certificate or diploma program. The college checks eligibility; the first term is paid back retroactively if you have a 3.5 GPA at the end of it.
amount_text: Full standard undergraduate tuition at the school you attend (up to 15 hours per term)
deadline_text: Apply before or during the term you enroll; ask your college's financial aid office for its cutoff
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia resident in a certificate or diploma program (not a degree program) and keep a 3.5 cumulative college GPA. Not available for dual enrollment. Grant hours are capped at 63 semester hours.

name: HOPE Career Grant
summary: Extra money on top of the HOPE Grant or Zell Miller Grant for students in high-demand technical programs, such as welding, nursing-related fields, truck driving and law enforcement. It helps pay costs beyond tuition.
how_to_apply: Enroll in an eligible program at a Georgia technical college and qualify for the HOPE Grant; the award is added for each eligible term. Ask your college's financial aid office to confirm your program is on the list.
amount_text: $125 to $500 per term for most programs; up to $1,100 for truck driving and up to $3,750 for basic law enforcement
deadline_text: Paid each term you are enrolled in an eligible program
other_requirements: Must be receiving the HOPE Grant or Zell Miller Grant and be enrolled in a program on the state's high-demand career list. Not available for dual enrollment.

name: Dual Enrollment
summary: Lets Georgia high school students take college classes for free while still in high school, earning both high school and college credit. It covers tuition, mandatory fees and required books for approved courses.
how_to_apply: Get admitted to a participating Georgia college, then complete the Dual Enrollment funding application on GAfutures with your high school counselor and the college. Apply before each term.
amount_text: Free tuition, mandatory fees and required books, up to 30 semester hours total (15 hours per term)
deadline_text: Before each term; check the college's dual enrollment deadline
other_requirements: 9th graders are not eligible. 10th graders may only take approved career (CTAE) courses at a technical college, or any approved course if they have a 1200 SAT or 26 ACT. 11th and 12th graders may take any approved course. Must attend an eligible Georgia public or private high school or home study program. Funding stops at 30 semester hours, and withdrawing from two courses ends eligibility.

name: Accelerated Career Education (ACE) Grant
summary: For public high school students on Georgia's Accelerated Career Diploma path who take a high-demand career program at a technical college. It covers tuition, waives fees and pays for required books.
how_to_apply: Talk with your high school counselor about the Accelerated Career Diploma, then enroll in an eligible program at a TCSG college. Funding is requested through GAfutures, much like Dual Enrollment.
amount_text: Standard tuition, mandatory fees waived, and required books, up to 15 semester hours per term
deadline_text: Offered every term; apply before the term starts
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia public high school student pursuing the Accelerated Career Diploma, in an associate of applied science, licensure diploma, or two related technical certificates on the High Demand Career List. Hours count toward the Dual Enrollment 30-hour cap.

name: DREAMS Scholarship
summary: Need-based aid for Pell Grant-eligible Georgia residents working on an associate or bachelor's degree at a University System of Georgia or technical college school. It helps fill the gap left after other grants.
how_to_apply: File the FAFSA and enroll at an eligible USG or TCSG college; the college decides who receives it and may have its own application. Complete the online Financial Toolkit sessions in your GAfutures account before the first payment.
amount_text: Up to $1,500 per term and $3,000 per year, limited to your unmet need
deadline_text: Set by each college; ask your financial aid office
other_requirements: Must be Pell Grant eligible, enrolled in at least 6 hours in an associate or bachelor's program at a USG or TCSG school, and keep a 2.0 college GPA. After the first term, students must do at least 60 hours of paid or unpaid work (jobs, internships, volunteering) each term. Funds are limited, so colleges award first to those who qualify early.

name: Georgia Foster Care Scholarship
summary: Pays college costs such as tuition, fees, books and housing for Georgia students who spent time in foster care with DFCS or were adopted from DFCS custody after age 14.
how_to_apply: Apply through GAfutures and your college's financial aid office before the term. Awards are first come, first served while funds last.
amount_text: Your direct college costs (tuition, fees, books, room and board), up to $30,000 a year
deadline_text: Apply early; awards are first come, first served
other_requirements: Must be under 26 and a Georgia resident, enrolled in at least 6 hours at an eligible Georgia college. Must meet one pathway: in DFCS foster care for at least 6 months after turning 14, currently in DFCS custody or its independent living program, adopted from DFCS after 14, or in a family receiving state-funded adoption services.

name: Georgia Public Service Memorial Grant
summary: Helps pay college costs for the children and spouses of Georgia public safety officers (police, firefighters, EMTs, paramedics, prison guards and others) or public school employees who were killed or permanently disabled in the line of duty.
how_to_apply: Fill out Part A of the application, have your college's financial aid office complete Part B, then upload it with documents about the incident through the GAfutures upload portal. You must reapply each year.
amount_text: Cost of attendance minus other aid, up to $18,000 a year and $72,000 total
deadline_text: No fixed date; awards are first come, first served, so apply early each year
other_requirements: Parent or spouse must have been a Georgia public safety officer permanently disabled or killed in the line of duty, or a public school employee killed or permanently disabled by an act of violence on the job. Must attend an eligible Georgia college.

name: Georgia HERO Scholarship
summary: For Georgia National Guard members and U.S. Military Reservists who served in a combat zone, and for their children and spouses. Helps pay for college at Georgia public or private schools.
how_to_apply: Fill out the HERO Scholarship form (linked from the GAfutures page) no later than two years after you become eligible, and renew each academic year.
amount_text: Up to $2,000 a year, up to $8,000 total
deadline_text: Within two years of becoming eligible; renew every year
other_requirements: Parent must have been a Georgia resident in the Georgia National Guard or U.S. Military Reserves deployed to a designated combat zone for at least 181 days (or evacuated for severe injury), with service starting on or after Feb. 1, 2003. Child must have been born before or within nine months of that service and been 25 or younger at the time. Must be a Georgia resident for 12 months before the term.

name: Inclusive Postsecondary Education (IPSE) Grant
summary: Helps students with intellectual disabilities pay tuition and program fees in an approved inclusive college program at schools such as UGA, Georgia Tech, Kennesaw State, Georgia State and others.
how_to_apply: Get admitted to an approved IPSE program at a participating college, then apply through that college and GAfutures. The college confirms your enrollment.
amount_text: Up to $13,000 a year at most four-year schools (amounts vary by college)
deadline_text: Set by each IPSE program; ask the college
other_requirements: Must have a qualifying intellectual disability, be a Georgia resident, and be enrolled in an approved IPSE program (e.g., Albany Tech, Berry, Columbus State, Georgia College, Georgia Tech, Georgia Southern, Georgia State, Kennesaw State, UGA).

name: University of North Georgia ROTC Grant
summary: A yearly grant for Georgia residents attending the University of North Georgia full time and taking part in its ROTC program.
how_to_apply: Enroll full time at UNG and join ROTC; apply through UNG and GAfutures each year.
amount_text: Up to $1,500 a year ($750 per fall and spring term)
deadline_text: Each academic year; check with UNG
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia resident, full-time undergraduate at UNG, and enrolled in ROTC each term paid. Cannot receive this and the Future Officers grant in the same term.

name: University of North Georgia ROTC Grant for Future Officers
summary: A larger yearly grant for UNG ROTC students who commit to becoming Army officers.
how_to_apply: Enroll full time at UNG in ROTC and apply through UNG and GAfutures; by the end of junior year you must sign a contract to accept an Army commission.
amount_text: Up to $4,000 a year ($2,000 per fall and spring term)
deadline_text: Each academic year; check with UNG
other_requirements: Same as the UNG ROTC Grant, plus a contract to accept a commission as an Army officer by the end of junior year.

name: Georgia Military College State Service Scholarship
sponsor: Georgia Student Finance Commission / Georgia Military College
summary: A two-year full-cost scholarship to Georgia Military College's Milledgeville campus for students who serve in the Georgia National Guard. It is technically a service-cancelable loan: you repay it with Guard service instead of money.
how_to_apply: File the FAFSA, then complete the GMC State Service application with an essay, photo, school recommendation and a nomination from your Georgia state legislator. Your counselor sends your transcript, senior schedule and SAT/ACT scores to GMC Admissions.
amount_text: Up to full cost of attendance (tuition, fees, room, meals, books, uniforms) minus other grants, for two years
deadline_text: Usually spring of senior year; confirm with GMC Admissions
other_requirements: Must serve four years in the Georgia National Guard (two while at GMC, two after) or repay the money as a loan. Georgia resident for 12 months, nominated by a member of the Georgia General Assembly, meet Guard health standards, and enroll full time.

name: University of North Georgia Military Service Scholarship
sponsor: Georgia Student Finance Commission / University of North Georgia
summary: A full four-year scholarship to the University of North Georgia's Corps of Cadets for students who will become part-time Army officers in the Georgia Army National Guard. It is a service-cancelable loan repaid through Guard service.
how_to_apply: Apply through UNG's online portal with an essay, school recommendation, transcript, SAT or ACT score, senior schedule, and a nomination form from a Georgia state legislator, and sign the promissory note.
amount_text: Full four years of tuition, fees, room, meals, books and uniforms
deadline_text: Senior year; check UNG's application page for the date
other_requirements: Must enlist in the Georgia Army National Guard, join UNG's Corps of Cadets, and commission as a second lieutenant after graduating; otherwise the money must be repaid. Georgia resident for 12 months, nominated by a Georgia legislator, strong high school record, and meet Guard health standards.

name: Georgia Foundation Scholarship for Agriculture
sponsor: Georgia Foundation for Agriculture (Georgia Farm Bureau)
summary: For Georgia high school seniors who plan to study agriculture, environmental sciences, family and consumer sciences, forestry or a related field at a Georgia college with an agriculture program.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Georgia Foundation for Agriculture's scholarship page by March 1 of senior year.
amount_text: Ten $3,000 awards; the top two applicants get an extra $1,500
deadline_text: March 1 of senior year
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia resident with high school leadership activities, majoring in an agriculture-related field at a USG school, Berry College, Emmanuel College, or another accredited Georgia college with an agriculture program. Must earn at least a 3.0 GPA in the first college semester; money is paid in the spring.

name: Georgia 4-H Foundation Scholarships
summary: A group of more than a dozen scholarships for Georgia 4-H members heading to college, including the Georgia 4-H Achievement Scholarship (for UGA's agriculture college), 4-H Dollars for 4-H Scholars, and need-based awards.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Georgia 4-H Foundation scholarship application; the 2027 application opens December 1, 2026. Ask your county 4-H agent for help.
amount_text: Varies by scholarship; Georgia 4-H awards over $50,000 a year in total
deadline_text: Application opens December 1; deadline usually in early spring
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia 4-H member. Most awards are for incoming college freshmen no older than 19 on January 1 of the application year. Some require a financial need statement, an agriculture or forestry major, or attending UGA, ABAC, or a USG college.

name: Georgia's Ford Dealers Scholarship (Georgia FFA Foundation)
summary: For Georgia FFA members who are graduating seniors planning to earn a college degree related to agriculture. About twenty awards are given each year.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Georgia Ford Dealers Scholarship application linked from the Georgia FFA post-secondary scholarships page in the spring of senior year.
amount_text: $1,000 (about twenty awards)
deadline_text: Usually late March or early April of senior year
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia FFA member and incoming college freshman planning an agriculture-related degree. Georgia FFA also offers the Growing America's Farmers Scholarship (eight $1,000 awards) for students going into production agriculture.

name: Nancy Penn Lyons Scholarship
summary: A renewable scholarship for strong Georgia high school seniors who are committed to community service.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta's online scholarship portal (opens in December) with your FAFSA Submission Summary, transcript, SAT or ACT report and an essay.
amount_text: Up to $6,000 a year for four years
deadline_text: Usually early March (2026 cycle ran Dec. 8 to March 2)
other_requirements: Must be a graduating Georgia high school senior with a commitment to community service. SAT score is reading plus math.

name: Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta General Scholarship
summary: One universal application that considers students for many named scholarship funds at the Atlanta-area community foundation, judged on grades, work, community involvement and financial need.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the foundation's scholarship portal and submit the universal application, essay (about 500 words), transcript, FAFSA Submission Summary and SAT/ACT report as PDFs.
amount_text: Varies by fund
deadline_text: Usually early March (2026 cycle ran Dec. 8 to March 2); no extensions
other_requirements: Must plan to enroll full time. Some funds are limited to students from certain towns or areas in metro Atlanta; read each fund's description in the portal.

name: Dream's Squared Scholarship
summary: For students with financial need and a GPA between 2.0 and 3.0 who are headed to a two- or four-year college full time. A good option for students who miss the cutoff for most merit awards.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta's online scholarship portal, which opens in December.
amount_text: Varies
deadline_text: Usually early March (2026 cycle closed March 2)
other_requirements: GPA must be between 2.0 and 3.0. Must be accepted to an accredited two- or four-year school and enroll full time.

name: Mayor's Youth Scholarship
sponsor: Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta / City of Atlanta
summary: For Atlanta Public Schools graduates and City of Atlanta residents going to a two- or four-year college. There is no minimum GPA, and Pell Grant recipients get priority.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta's online scholarship portal, which opens in December.
amount_text: Varies
deadline_text: Usually early March (2026 cycle closed March 2)
other_requirements: Must be an Atlanta Public Schools graduate, a City of Atlanta resident, or recommended by a City of Atlanta employee. Must not have received it before and must be accepted to a two- or four-year school.

name: Community Foundation of Central Georgia Scholarships
summary: One universal online application that matches Middle Georgia students to many local scholarship funds, some based on financial need.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the foundation's online scholarship portal and complete the universal application with a transcript, a recommendation letter and a photo, plus any extra questions for scholarships you are matched to.
amount_text: Varies by fund
deadline_text: Opens December 15 and closes February 28 at noon
other_requirements: Most funds are for students from Macon and the surrounding Middle Georgia counties; each fund has its own rules.

name: North Georgia Community Foundation Scholarships
summary: One application for more than 80 local scholarship funds for students in North Georgia (including Hall, Forsyth, Habersham and nearby counties). Recently it gave 327 awards totaling about $823,000.
how_to_apply: Apply through the NGCF online scholarship portal during the winter application window.
amount_text: Varies by fund
deadline_text: Usually mid-January to early March (2026 cycle ran Jan. 15 to March 2)
other_requirements: Most funds are limited to students from certain North Georgia counties or high schools; check each fund's rules in the portal.

name: Community Foundation for the CSRA Scholarships
sponsor: Community Foundation for the Central Savannah River Area (Augusta)
summary: Local scholarships for graduating seniors in the Augusta area, including awards for STEM, skilled trades, agriculture and Eagle Scouts.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the foundation's online scholarship portal and apply to the funds you qualify for; your counselor and references upload documents through emailed links.
amount_text: About $500 to $2,000 depending on the fund
deadline_text: Most deadlines are around March 20 each year; some in May or July
other_requirements: Must live in or graduate from a high school in Burke, Columbia, McDuffie, Richmond or Warren County, Georgia (or Aiken County, SC). Each fund has its own rules.

name: Walter Harrison Scholarship
sponsor: Georgia EMC (through local electric membership cooperatives)
summary: A $1,000 scholarship for students whose home gets power from a Georgia electric membership cooperative (EMC), for any accredited two- or four-year college or technical school in Georgia.
how_to_apply: Get the application from your local EMC (for example Cobb, Jackson or Walton EMC) and submit it to them by their deadline; each EMC forwards finalists to a statewide committee.
deadline_text: Usually early February (Cobb EMC's 2026 deadline was Feb. 6); dates vary by EMC
other_requirements: Primary home must be served by a participating Georgia EMC. Must attend an accredited Georgia college, university or technical school. Selection looks at GPA, SAT scores, honors and financial need.

name: Georgia Press Educational Foundation Scholarship
summary: For Georgia students with financial need and an interest in newspaper journalism who will attend a Georgia college. Seniors in high school may apply.
how_to_apply: Download the application from the Georgia Press Association website and email it to the foundation by February 1; a counselor, principal, professor or Georgia Press member should recommend you.
amount_text: Varies; paid directly to your college for tuition
deadline_text: February 1 (the page lists Feb. 1, 2027 for the 2027-28 cycle)
other_requirements: A parent must have been a Georgia resident for two years, or the student for three years. Must attend a Georgia college or university and show prior interest in newspaper journalism. Reapply each year.

name: SPJ Georgia High School Scholarship
sponsor: Society of Professional Journalists, Georgia Chapter
summary: Three $500 awards for Georgia public high school seniors who plan to major in journalism and are interested in digital, broadcast or podcast storytelling.
how_to_apply: Download the application guidelines from the SPJ Georgia website and follow the submission steps; the chapter posts the call for applications in winter.
amount_text: $500 (three winners)
deadline_text: Usually winter to spring of senior year; check the guidelines
other_requirements: Must attend a public high school in Georgia and plan to declare journalism as a college major.

name: GAE Foundation High School Senior Scholarship for Future Teachers
summary: For Georgia public high school seniors who plan to major in education at a Georgia college or university.
how_to_apply: Download the fillable application from the GAE Foundation grants page; applications are posted each October.
amount_text: Not stated
deadline_text: Applications open in October; check the form for the due date
other_requirements: Must graduate this year from a Georgia public high school and attend a Georgia college or university as an education major.

name: Hispanic Alliance GA Scholarship
sponsor: Hispanic Alliance GA (administered by Scholarship America)
summary: For Georgia high school seniors headed to a two- or four-year college or technical school full time, judged on grades, leadership, community involvement, work, goals and financial need.
how_to_apply: Apply online through Scholarship America when the program opens, uploading a full transcript and SAT/ACT scores if they aren't on it. Winners are told in late January.
amount_text: $1,500, renewable for one more year (up to 8 awards)
deadline_text: Usually fall to early winter of senior year (currently closed; 2026 details listed as tentative)
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia resident and enroll full time for the whole upcoming year. The page does not say applicants must be Hispanic.

name: John W. Youtsey Memorial Scholarship
summary: For Georgia residents who are Hemophilia of Georgia clients with hemophilia, von Willebrand disease or another inherited bleeding disorder and are going to college, technical school or a professional program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online pre-qualification form by mid-April; if you qualify, you'll get the full application by email.
amount_text: Varies; the program has given more than 500 scholarships worth over $2 million
deadline_text: Pre-qualification due mid-April (April 15 in 2026)
other_requirements: Must have an inherited bleeding disorder, be a Hemophilia of Georgia client, and have lived in Georgia for at least one year. Recipients volunteer at least 12 hours with Hemophilia of Georgia.

name: Georgia Transplant Foundation Academic Scholarship
summary: For Georgia students who are organ transplant recipients, living donors, or the children, parents or siblings of a transplant recipient, going to college or technical school.
how_to_apply: Apply online or mail the paper application with transcripts, your acceptance letter, a personal statement of up to three pages and two recommendation letters, postmarked by May 1.
amount_text: $1,000 a year, renewable for up to four years
deadline_text: Postmarked by May 1 each year
other_requirements: Must be a Georgia resident and a transplant recipient, a dependent or parent of a recipient, a living donor, or a sibling of a recipient (sibling and recipient both 22 or younger).

name: GSGA Foundation Yates Scholarship
summary: A renewable, need-based scholarship for students who work at a GSGA member golf club in Georgia (golf operations, course maintenance or clubhouse), or whose parent does. In 2026-27 the foundation gave about $447,000 to 80 scholars.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the GSGA Foundation scholarship portal between September 1 and March 1; finalists are interviewed.
amount_text: Varies; renewable through the fourth year of college
deadline_text: Application window September 1 to March 1 (open now for 2027-28)
other_requirements: Must be an employee of a GSGA member club, or the dependent of one. Georgia schools must be HOPE-eligible; out-of-state schools must be accredited. For a first bachelor's degree only.

name: Georgia ProStart Invitational Scholarships
summary: High school ProStart culinary and restaurant management teams compete statewide, and the top three teams in each contest win college scholarships. More than $150,000 was awarded in 2025.
how_to_apply: Join your high school's ProStart program and compete in the Georgia ProStart Invitational, held each winter; your ProStart teacher registers the team.
amount_text: Varies by placement
deadline_text: Competition held in late winter each year
other_requirements: Must be on a Georgia high school ProStart team and place in the top three in the Culinary or Management competition.

name: The Eichholz Law Firm Scholarship for High School Seniors
summary: Four $1,000 awards for high school seniors in the Savannah area who are active in community service and extracurriculars.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with a 500-word original essay about your commitment to community service and activities; the application usually opens in spring.
amount_text: $1,000 (four awards)
deadline_text: Usually late May (2026 deadline was May 29)
other_requirements: Must be a senior in Chatham, Effingham, Bryan or Liberty County, Georgia (or Allendale, Beaufort, Hampton or Jasper County, SC) and attend an accredited college in Georgia or South Carolina.
